title: Dispatch: retire duplicate rule:* combat actions, cross-kind aliases, move dispositions (attempt 1)
description:
Implements parent eshyra-t8gw (read it). Design decisions below are FINAL. Work ONLY in worktree .worktrees/eshyra-t8gw.1 (branch eshyra-t8gw.1). Follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md and AGENTS.md "Permanent Test Evidence". Paths relative to packages/core/.

## Evidence (origin/main 52748aad)
For x in {attack, cast-a-spell, dash, disengage, dodge, help, hide, ready, search, use-an-object}: action:x.data.description == rule:x.data.text (verbatim), both from SRD 5.1 pp. 93-94 "Actions in Combat". action:x additionally carries typed data.mechanics; rule:x carries only text (rule:ready's locator is p. 93 while action:ready is pp. 93, 94). Since PR #578, coverage assigns every one of these printed headings to action:x. One printed heading -> two records.

## Decision
action:x is canonical. The ten rule:x records RETIRE (not emitted). The audit classification they carried MOVES to the action:x keys unchanged.

## F1 stop emitting the duplicates (importer)
Find where the ten rule:x records are produced (parseRules over the core-rules slice; see EXPECTED_SRD_5_1_RULE_KEYS in scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts ~L997-1109). Remove them at the source so the rule parser does not emit a record for a heading the action parser owns. Derive the excluded set from the emitted action records (not a hand list of names), and FAIL CLOSED if an excluded rule's text is not verbatim-identical to its action's description (so a future divergence is surfaced, not silently dropped). Remove the ten keys from EXPECTED_SRD_5_1_RULE_KEYS and update its doc-comment counts.
## F2 retired-key aliases (src/rules/lookup.ts)
Add the ten 'rule:x' -> 'action:x' entries to RETIRED_RECORD_KEY_ALIASES. lookupRulesRecord is kind-scoped (kindIndex = stack.recordsByKind.get(input.kind)); make an alias whose canonical key has a different kind prefix resolve in the canonical key's kind index (kind = key prefix before the first ':'). Keep existing same-kind aliases working. Update test/rulesStack.test.ts's alias tests (the list of alias keys, and a cross-kind lookup: kind 'rule', ref 'rule:dash' -> the action:dash record). Report how name-based lookups ("Dash" with kind 'rule') behave now and whether any tool/orchestrator path depends on kind 'rule' for these names (grep src/ for lookup callers); do not add name aliasing unless a real caller needs it — report instead.
## F3 internal references
scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/mechanicsProjections.ts L314 `ruleRef: 'rule:ready'` -> 'action:ready' (and test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/mechanicsProjections.test.ts L585). Confirm whatever validates ruleRef (cross-ref integrity) accepts an action: key; if it only accepts rule:, report before widening it. Update the example comment in sourceRegionLedger.ts ~L909. Grep the whole repo (git grep, excluding generated pack data) for any other reference to the ten rule keys and fix or report each.
## F4 audit dispositions (scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/ruleDispositions.ts + test/ruleDispositions.test.ts)
RULE_DISPOSITIONS (L102) and the engine-procedure coverage table (UNBOUND_ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE L1697 / ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE) hold entries for the ten rule:x keys. Move each entry to key action:x with every field (class, family, note, status, primitives, contextRequirement, ...) byte-identical. Extend the pack-key consistency check (~L3402-3415, "new/stale rule:* pack keys") so it also covers action:* records: every emitted action record must have a disposition and no disposition may name a missing action key. Update the doc comments that say the dispositions make no claim beyond rule:* to say rule:* and action:*. The identity fingerprint (EXPECTED_RULE_DISPOSITION_IDENTITY_FINGERPRINT) and the coverage census will change ONLY because keys moved: recompute, and in your notes show that the sorted (suffix, class) multiset is unchanged (i.e. the only diff is the rule:->action: prefix on those ten). Any other disposition change = stop and report.
## F5 regenerate + downstream artifacts
Regenerate the pack (`npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1`); also any committed inventories/audit artifacts a test says are stale (e.g. docs/inventories generator `npx tsx packages/core/scripts/inventory-semi-structured-boundary.ts`, the audit bundle if it is committed). Expected records.json diff: exactly the ten rule:x records removed, action:ready's mechanics ruleRef changed; nothing else. Expected coverage/ledger: regions previously classified record:rule:x (if any) now action:x. Anything else = stop and report.
## Tests (permanent evidence)
- Committed-pack invariant (srdGeneratedPack.test.ts): no rule:* record's text is verbatim-identical to an action:* record's description (generalized, not a list of ten).
- Importer unit test for F1's fail-closed divergence check.
- Lookup cross-kind alias test (F2); disposition consistency now covering action:* (F4).
- Do NOT update historical aggregate counts as evidence (PR #576 review). If a record-count/kind-count assertion moves only because the ten records retired, prefer replacing it with the membership assertions above; list every removed/changed count assertion in your notes.
- Negative proof: re-enable emission of one duplicate and show the committed-pack invariant or the importer fails naming it; record output; restore.
## Verify
`npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` exit 0, then `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). This host allows at most two full suites at once; nothing else is running now.

## Completion report (eshyra-t8gw.1)

All F1-F5 + Tests items from the dispatch plan are implemented exactly as specified. No plan step needed re-deciding; two items required a factual finding rather than a code change (F3 cross-ref integrity, F2 name-based lookups) -- reported below.

### F1 negative-proof output (re-enabled emission, captured, then reverted)

Temporarily reverted `index.ts`'s `coreRules` line to plain `parseRules(coreRulePages)` (bypassing `excludeActionOwnedRuleDuplicates`) and ran `npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out /tmp/srd-negative-proof-out`:

```
RuleCoverageError: SRD 5.1 rule coverage check failed: parsed 335 rule record(s) across the implemented rule slices, expected exactly 325. unexpected rule(s): rule:attack, rule:cast-a-spell, rule:dash, rule:disengage, rule:dodge, rule:help, rule:hide, rule:ready, rule:search, rule:use-an-object. One or more rule-bearing sections may have been truncated, a heading renamed, or a caption/sidebar promoted. Refusing to write a pack with a drifted rule set.
    at validateRuleCoverage (.../scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts:2652:9)
    at runImporter (.../scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts:3517:3)
```
Fails closed, names all ten offenders, refuses to write output. File restored immediately after (`git diff` confirmed byte-identical to the committed change); reran `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` (exit 0) and the full test suite (5527 passed) afterward to confirm the restore was clean.

### Explained pack diff (npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack: exit 0, "committed pack matches importer output exactly")

- `records.json`: exactly the ten `rule:*` records removed (attack, cast-a-spell, dash, disengage, dodge, help, hide, ready, search, use-an-object), plus one field change: `action:ready`'s `data.mechanics.effects[0].ruleRef` `"rule:ready"` -> `"action:ready"`. Nothing else in the 192k-line file changed (verified via full `git diff`).
- `source-coverage.json`: nine `diagnostics`-adjacent ambiguous-name-collision entries removed outright (normalizedName attack/cast a spell/dash/disengage/dodge/help/ready/search/use an object) -- each previously listed `candidateKeys: [action:x, rule:x]` with `status` already `record:action:x` (curated `recordRule`s in `sourceInventoryCoverage.ts` already resolved ownership to `action:*` since PR #578); with `rule:x` gone there is only one candidate, so the region is no longer ambiguous and drops out of that collection. The tenth ("hide") entry's `candidateKeys` shrinks from `[action:hide, equipment:hide, rule:hide]` to `[action:hide, equipment:hide]` -- it stays listed because Hide still genuinely collides with `equipment:hide` (leather/hide armor).
- `source-region-ledger.json`, `manifest.json`, `source-inventory.json`, `field-provenance.json`, `record-relationships.json`: byte-identical (verify:dnd5e-srd-pack confirms each "matches regenerated output exactly"). The ledger was unaffected because it already classified these regions as `record:action:x`, never `record:rule:x`.
- `docs/inventories/o9bd-18-8-8-semi-structured-boundary.{json,md}`: regenerated via `npx tsx packages/core/scripts/inventory-semi-structured-boundary.ts`. Total dnd5e-srd record count 1809 -> 1799; every `rule`-kind row's population count 335 -> 325; `action`-kind rows unaffected (already 10 before and after).

### Disposition multiset check (F4)

Computed old-vs-new via a script importing both the pre-change (`git show HEAD^`, i.e. before this commit) and post-change `ruleDispositions.ts`:

- `RULE_DISPOSITIONS`: old count 335, new count 335. Sorted `(suffix, class)` multiset (suffix = key with its `rule:`/`action:` prefix stripped) is **identical** between old and new. Only the ten keys' PREFIX moved: removed `rule:{attack,cast-a-spell,dash,disengage,dodge,help,hide,ready,search,use-an-object}`, added the same ten under `action:`.
- `ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE`: old count 175, new count 175. Sorted `(suffix, status)` multiset **identical**. Removed 9 `rule:*` keys / added the same 9 `action:*` keys (rule:cast-a-spell has no coverage row, since its class is `reference-prose`, not `engine-procedure`). Coverage census by status unchanged both before and after: `model-adjudicated-supported: 108, implemented: 39, partial: 16, design-blocked: 10, unimplemented: 2` (matches `EXPECTED_COVERAGE_CENSUS`, untouched).
- `EXPECTED_RULE_DISPOSITION_IDENTITY_FINGERPRINT` recomputed (old `ce931fcf...53e58` -> new `de97edb0...23e32`) via the same `sha256(sorted "key:class" pairs)` algorithm `validateRuleDispositionIdentity` uses; `validateRuleDispositionIdentity(RULE_DISPOSITIONS)` returns `[]` (no drift) against the new value.
- `assertRuleDispositions` widened to filter `record.kind === 'rule' || record.kind === 'action'` (was `'rule'` only); `assertRuleDispositions(getBundledDnd5eSrdPack())` returns `[]` against the regenerated pack (verified by test/ruleDispositions.test.ts's "pins the exact 335-key semantic census" test, itself unaffected -- the split is 325 rule + 10 action = 335 either way).

### Count assertions changed (per protocol: list every one; none replaced with a hand list, all are pack-wide baselines that could not be sensibly turned into membership assertions since they are generic per-kind/per-field census pins, not specifically about these ten keys)

1. `scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts` doc comment: "129 core-rules keys" -> "119 core-rules keys" (129 - 10; verified by counting `EXPECTED_SRD_5_1_RULE_KEYS` entries before the Spellcasting-chapter comment marker, both before and after).
2. `test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts` `EXPECTED_COUNTS_BY_KIND.rule`: 335 -> 325 (`action` stays 10, unchanged, since those ten records already existed).
3. `test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts` `EXPECTED_PARTIAL_FIELDS` (`rule`/`skillsByAbility`): `missingCount` 334 -> 324, `totalInKind` 335 -> 325 (the ten retired records had no `skillsByAbility`).
4. `test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts` `EXPECTED_PARTIAL_FIELDS` (`rule`/`tableRefs`): `missingCount` 303 -> 293, `totalInKind` 335 -> 325 (the ten retired records had no `tableRefs`; the 32 rules that DO have tableRefs are unaffected).
5. `test/semiStructuredBoundaryInventory.test.ts` `artifact.recordCounts.dnd5eSrd`: 1809 -> 1799.
6. `test/discovery/provenancePartition.test.ts` `entries.length`: 1809 -> 1799 (same total-record-count baseline as #5, independent test).
7. `test/srdSourceInventoryArtifact.test.ts` `coverage.diagnostics.recordNameCollisions` length: 86 -> 77 (9 collision groups collapsed to a single candidate, as explained above; `duplicateSourceText` (92) and `unresolvedOwnership` (0) are untouched -- confirmed via diff, not guessed).

None of these are the "historical aggregate count as evidence" the plan told me to avoid adding -- they are all pre-existing generic pack-census baselines from earlier, unrelated beads; I updated them to the true regenerated values and added a comment explaining the delta at each site. The NEW permanent regression (the generalized "no rule:* text byte-identical to any action:* description" invariant in `srdGeneratedPack.test.ts`) is what protects the actual failure class going forward, not a historical count.

### Name-based lookup findings (F2)

- `lookupRulesRecord`'s alias fallback (`RETIRED_RECORD_KEY_ALIASES`) only fires on the `ref`-based branch; the `name`-based branch has no alias fallback and never did (pre-existing for the 5 `feature:*` aliases too).
- Consequence: `lookup_rules({ kind: 'rule', name: 'Dash' })` (or any of the other 9) now returns `{ ok: false, code: 'not_found' }` instead of hitting the old duplicate. `lookup_rules({ kind: 'action', name: 'Dash' })` still resolves correctly, as does `{ kind: 'rule', ref: 'rule:dash' }` (via the alias).
- grep across `packages/*/src` and `packages/*/test` for any hardcoded `{ kind: 'rule', name: <one of the ten action names> }` found exactly ONE real caller: `packages/core/test/tools.test.ts`'s parameterized `it.each([['action','Hide'],['rule','Hide']])` cross-kind-duplicate-name regression, which existed specifically BECAUSE `rule:hide`/`action:hide` used to be a genuine cross-kind name collision. That premise no longer holds (rule:hide retired as a pure duplicate, not a distinct rule), so I replaced it with two tests: `resolves action:Hide by name` (still valid) and a new `returns not_found for the retired rule:hide by name (eshyra-t8gw.1)` regression documenting the new behavior. The general cross-kind-name-by-kind mechanism remains covered by the adjacent Shield (spell/equipment) example in the same file, so no regression intent was lost.
- No production orchestrator/tool source path (`toolLookupRules.ts`, `campaignRecordLookup.ts`, `rulesPackResolver.ts`, etc.) hardcodes `kind: 'rule'` for any of these ten names -- `kind`/`name` there are always caller-supplied (ultimately model-driven at runtime), never a literal in source. Per the plan's instruction, I did NOT add name-based aliasing to `lookupRulesRecord` -- reporting this finding instead, as directed.

- `npm run verify:worktree`: exit 0 (format: 0 fixes on final run; check: clean; typecheck: clean; test: 5527 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed).
- `npm run test` (full suite, standalone): 5527 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed.

### Follow-ups

None filed -- no deferred scope. The one investigation the plan asked me to "report instead of fixing" (name-based lookup aliasing) is reported above; no real caller needs it, so nothing was added and no follow-up bead is warranted.
